title: Hidradenitis suppurativa
summary: A chronic inflammatory disease of hair follicles in the armpits, groin and under the breasts, with recurrent painful nodules, abscesses, tunnels and scarring. Treat early and refer before scarring sets in.

glance.think: Recurrent painful ‘boils’ in the same flexural sites, with double comedones, tunnels or rope-like scars.
glance.engine: Follicular occlusion and rupture, then IL-17/TNF-driven inflammation; obesity, smoking and genetics add risk. Not an infection or a hygiene problem.
glance.backbone: Weight and smoking support, antiseptic washes, analgesia; topical clindamycin for mild disease; tetracycline course; early dermatology referral for biologics (NICE TA).
glance.never_miss: Under-treatment and delay: scarring and tunnels are irreversible. Also depression, and SCC in long-standing perianal disease.

what: Chronic autoinflammatory disease of **apocrine-bearing** / intertriginous skin (acne inversa). Painful deep nodules and abscesses that may form **draining sinus tracts** and irreversible scarring. Not caused by poor hygiene; not contagious. Marked quality-of-life and comorbidity burden.
cause: Follicular **occlusion → rupture →** innate immune cascade → tunnels and fibrosis. Drivers: genetics (~⅓ family history), obesity/friction, **smoking**, hormones, microbial dysbiosis. Female predominance (~3:1) in Western cohorts; onset typically after puberty (2nd–3rd decade).

ol: **Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp** (perifolliculitis capitis abscedens et suffodiens)

cause: **Tetrad** adds **pilonidal disease**. Syndromic overlap possible (e.g. PASH) — specialist territory.

list: Open/closed comedones (often **paired/"tombstone"**), painful firm nodules, abscesses, **draining sinuses**, rope-like scars.
Sites: **axillae**, groin, inframammary/submammary, buttocks, perianal/perineal, neck.
Day 1 vignette: recurrent axillary lumps since puberty → coalescent inflamed nodules, sinus tracts, pus, fibrosis ± smaller indurated nodules.

head: Stage
Meaning
rows: Single or multiple abscesses **without** sinus tracts or scarring
Recurrent abscesses **with** sinus tracts and scarring (separated by normal skin)
Diffuse involvement with **multiple interconnected** sinuses/abscesses across the region

features: Once scarring/sinuses exist, Hurley stage does not “step down” with medical therapy alone. Dynamic scores (IHS4, HiSCR) used more in secondary care/trials.
Day 1 consensus in forum: **at least Hurley II** (sinuses + scarring after failed long antibiotic courses).
diagnosis: Clinical — modified Dessau criteria (typical lesions + typical sites + chronicity/recurrence ≥2 flares in 6 months). Swabs often negative or colonised (supportive if sterile abscess picture). Biopsy rarely needed (exclude SCC in chronic ulcerated anogenital disease). Ultrasound/MRI for extent when planning surgery.

head: Look-alike
Distinguishing clues
rows: Discrete pointing abscesses; less bridging tunnels/rope scars; culture may grow Staph
Single cystic lesion; no multi-site comedonal disease
GI symptoms, fistulae; refer IBD work-up

management: Themes from DermNet/BAD HS guideline (Ingram et al.) and forum secondary-care commentary:

list: **Educate:** not infectious, not “dirt”; validate pain and QoL.
**Lifestyle:** smoking cessation; weight management; loose clothing; gentle antiseptic washes (e.g. chlorhexidine) as adjunct; wound dressings that don’t tear skin.
**Topical (mild disease):** clindamycin 1% BD to active lesions (short adjunct).

**Oral antibiotics (immunomodulatory courses, not one-off “boil” scripts):** tetracycline-class (e.g. doxycycline/lymecycline) often first medical step for mild–moderate disease — typically reviewed ~12 weeks; follow local antimicrobial stewardship.
**Screen comorbidities:** metabolic syndrome, diabetes, PCOS, CVD risk, depression/anxiety.
**Refer dermatology early** for Hurley **II–III**, failed primary-care antibiotics, multi-site disease, or diagnostic doubt — waiting lists are long; do not delay.

management.h: Specialist / secondary care (know when to escalate)

list: Combination **clindamycin + rifampicin** (typically up to ~12 weeks) for more severe/refractory disease — specialist initiation/monitoring (interactions, resistance, contraception counselling).
Other medical: short steroid rescue for flares; acitretin (males / non-fertile females); dapsone; metformin/anti-androgens in selected women — specialist.

**Biologics (specialist only):** UK-licensed options include **adalimumab** (usually first biologic), **secukinumab**, and (more recently) **bimekizumab** — for inadequate control after conventional therapy. Pre-biologic infection screen (CXR, BBV, etc.). Pregnancy plans constrain many options.
**Surgery:** incision & drainage = temporary relief only (almost always recurs); **deroofing**, local excision, or wider excision for chronic tunnels — combine with medical/lifestyle care.

red_flags: Fluctuant abscess with **systemic upset**: same-day drainage.
**Hurley II–III** disease (tunnels, scarring) or failure of a 12-week tetracycline course: refer to dermatology for systemic or biologic therapy.
Low mood or suicidal thoughts: HS has a high psychological burden.
Chronic non-healing ulcer within long-standing perianal or buttock HS: exclude **SCC**.
pearls: Stop calling every axillary lump a “boil” after the third recurrence in the same fold — think HS.
Document **Hurley stage**, sites, smoking, BMI, prior antibiotics.
Pregnancy/breastfeeding intent changes antibiotic, retinoid, and biologic choices — ask early.
Abscess drainage alone is not disease-modifying.
